claim: A combined Rydberg vapor cell + OPM 'quantum tricorder' built within a $50k independent-researcher budget can achieve: (a) SI-traceable RF field calibration from 100 MHz to 20 GHz at sensitivity ~500 nV/cm/sqrt(Hz) (10x below SOTA but peer-reviewable), and (b) DC-100 Hz magnetic sensing at 10 fT/sqrt(Hz) — but these two modalities cannot share a single compact chassis without electromagnetic cross-contamination from the Rydberg laser system.
confidence_rationale: Medium confidence. The individual modality claims are grounded in published SOTA (PAPER-2026-053, HW-2026-036): Rydberg EIT-AT at 500 nV/cm/sqrt(Hz) is achievable with a single ECDL pair and is 10x worse than best SOTA but scientifically meaningful; OPM at 10 fT/sqrt(Hz) is commercially available from QuSpin. The integration claim (they cannot share a chassis) is based on well-understood electromagnetic interference physics: the Rydberg probe laser (780 nm for Rb, ~5 mW optical power) generates photon shot noise and stray fields that would dominate over fT-level magnetic signals at kHz frequencies. Multiple sources converge on the SWaP reality (HW-2026-033 Tiqker: 30L/30kg for the laser system alone).
test_design: 1. Rydberg modality: Purchase one Rb vapor cell ($3k), one 780nm ECDL laser ($15k used/refurbished), one 480nm coupling laser ($15k used/refurbished), lock-in amplifier, photodetector. Perform EIT-AT spectroscopy at a known RF frequency (e.g., 6.9 GHz targeting Rb |50D_5/2> Rydberg state). Calibrate against a calibrated signal generator. Measure sensitivity floor (nV/cm/sqrt(Hz)) at 5 frequencies across 1-20 GHz. Report SI-traceable calibration curve. Estimated cost: $35k. 2. OPM modality: Purchase one QuSpin QZFM Gen-3 ($20k). Measure noise floor in same lab space with Rydberg laser system powered on vs off. Quantify electromagnetic interference at DC-1000 Hz. 3. Electromagnetic isolation test: Place OPM sensor at 0.5m, 1m, 2m from Rydberg vapor cell setup. Measure OPM noise floor as function of Rydberg laser power (0-5 mW) and chopping frequency. Determine minimum physical separation for OPM noise floor < 20 fT/sqrt(Hz). 4. Report: If minimum separation exceeds 1m, the two modalities cannot coexist in a portable chassis. If separation < 30cm is achievable with shielding, a combined portable system is feasible.
refutation_criteria: The 'cannot share chassis' sub-claim is refuted if OPM noise floor < 20 fT/sqrt(Hz) is maintained with Rydberg laser system operating at < 30cm separation with passive mu-metal shielding. The overall dual-modality claim is refuted if either: (a) Rydberg sensitivity at 500 nV/cm/sqrt(Hz) is not achievable with $35k laser budget (i.e., requires optical locking precision beyond used ECDL specs), OR (b) OPM 10 fT/sqrt(Hz) is not maintained in a non-shielded room (ambient noise > 10 fT/sqrt(Hz) is the true limit in typical lab spaces).
hardware_required: Rb vapor cell ($3k), 780nm ECDL ($15k refurbished), 480nm coupling laser ($15k refurbished), lock-in amplifier + photodetector ($5k), QuSpin QZFM Gen-3 OPM ($20k), RF signal generator ($5k), mu-metal shielding panels ($2k). Total: ~$65k (slightly above $50k budget — requires used laser market sourcing or university surplus). No cryogenics, no cleanroom.

feasibility_notes.hardware: 780nm ECDL: Toptica DL Pro used market ~$12-15k. 480nm: Toptica TA-SHG Pro used ~$18k or build from 960nm ECDL + SHG crystal (~$15k total). Rb vapor cell: Precision Glassblowing ~$3k. QuSpin OPM: $20k. Lock-in amplifier (SR830): $3k used. Total: ~$53-58k — marginally over $50k, achievable via university surplus or one borrowed laser from collaborator. Time to first EIT signal: 4-8 weeks post-laser acquisition.
feasibility_notes.circuit: N/A — this is a classical photonics + atomic physics experiment, no quantum circuit required.
feasibility_notes.math: EIT-AT sensitivity theory: well-established, PAPER-2026-056 gives Fisher-information-based sensitivity framework. EMI cross-contamination: OPM sensitivity peaks at DC-1kHz; laser current modulation noise (from ECDL servo electronics) typically in 10Hz-100kHz band — direct overlap. Mu-metal shielding attenuation: ~40-60 dB at 100 Hz for 1mm mu-metal sheet. Achievable physical separation for <20 fT noise from laser electronics: estimated 0.5-2m with shielding (needs experimental verification — this IS the hypothesis).
feasibility_notes.resource: Budget marginally exceeds $50k cap. Reducing to one ECDL pair (780nm probe only, 480nm coupling borrowed or skipped) allows EIT demonstration at ~$40k total. Single-photon EIT gives coarser sensitivity but still peer-reviewable RF calibration result. The EMI isolation study has zero additional hardware cost beyond what is already required.

pipeline_provenance.conjecture_stage: Generated from the 'quantum tricorder' framing in Tier 1 findings. The hypothesis reframes the Infleqtion SqyWire marketing claim into a falsifiable engineering question: what can a researcher actually build with $50k? The claim about electromagnetic cross-contamination is the novel scientific contribution — no paper has explicitly characterized OPM noise degradation from co-located Rydberg laser systems. This creates a publishable negative result if the cross-contamination is severe, and a publishable positive result if shielding solves it. Both outcomes advance the field. The individual modality capabilities (Rydberg EIT-AT, OPM magnetometry) are well-established; the integration question is the gap.
